items.gist: The passage derives the varṇa-set from kṣobha and yoni, distinguishing bhedābheda and the svaramaya origin of letters.
It explains vyañjana as dependent on svara, with six devatās and a lunar bodily form.
It distinguishes bhoktṛ and bhogya, locating bhogyatā in the mother and relating it to anuttara.

items.topic: triad of six and full power
items.gist: The six are reduced to a triad, identified with Bhairava's supreme light and the full power of the Lord.
Vimarśa is the single essence; from it arise śabdarāśi, mātṛkā, and Mālinī.
Śiva as parent and visarga are explained through parāmarśa and the withdrawal of the universe into anuttara.
The Triśikā's compacted power is related to consciousness, and one supreme form of Bhairava pervades.
Ānandaśakti appears in sweet song and touch, leading to cittaviśrānti.
It describes orientation toward objects, cittasaṃbodhana, and cittapralayana as śāmbhava visarga.
Three visargas are distinguished: cittaviśrānti, cittasaṃbodha, and cittapralaya.
Kuṇḍalinī as bīja and jīva is connected with varṇas, visarga, and bindu.
The guru's mark is given, and all things with initial and final letters are seen as mantra.
Agni, sun, and moon are related to vīrya, prajā, and the universal form of visarga.
Mātṛkā becomes Mālinī, and the single power takes yāmala form.
Pratyavamarśa manifests as paśyantī, madhyamā, and vaikharī, with paśyantī's gross and subtle forms.
